summary: The Queen walked the Long Walk with her lady-in-waiting, taking a private, low-profile outing that allowed her to reflect away from public ceremony.
Household prepared to keep the Queen's absence low-key; the kitchen prepared a cold tray (sliced cold chicken, open sandwiches and fruit) as provision during her walk.
The Queen opened her journal and wrote a short note after returning from the walk; the act closed the private interlude and altered her view of the day.
Arrival at Windsor station: a train from London brings the actress; press and fans gather; the manager takes press-telegrams and arranges privacy.
Manager collects and pockets press-telegrams distributed at the telegraph table, intending that they be answered from the cottage.
The party travels by black saloon with rear curtains from the station to the guest cottage; the actress keeps to herself, occupying her hands with a folded script.
Arrival at the guest cottage: driver unloads luggage, manager checks the front path, actress steps inside seeking ordinary privacy.
Driver guides press and junior porter back toward the edge of the platform, using practiced gestures to control proximity.
char-neighbor observed a black saloon with curtains drawn, the driver closing the door and an actress stepping from a carriage; he took these details back to the teashop.
The confidante paused outside the teashop, checked her watch and telegrams, entered briefly to make enquiries, then left to arrange matters elsewhere.
char-neighbor reported to teashop patrons what he had seen about the arrival; his telling set the town's conversation in motion.
A radio on a high shelf tuned to the county bulletin murmured a cricket score while the proprietor set out tea and sponge, marking the shop's quotidian background noise.
After leaving the teashop, char-neighbor buttoned his overcoat and walked toward the castle gates intending to look for the actress.
